title: Cross-language SDK Cookbook & Migration Changelog Pipeline
creator: Ayesha Kumar
description: Deliver a cross-language SDK cookbook (Python, TypeScript, Go) that showcases recommended patterns for retries, streaming ergonomics, and feature parity between v1->v2 SDKs. Build an automated changelog pipeline that maps code-level breaking changes to example transformations and produces ready-to-review PRs and changelog fragments. Goal: reduce migration friction for customers and provide canonical examples for the docs site and SDK repos.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Cookbook pages for Python, TS, Go with at least 6 canonical recipes: simple text generation, streaming chat (generator/async iterator), idempotent retries for requests with side effects, resumable stream consumption with backpressure, embedding batching with caching, and function/tool-calling example.
2) Migration pipeline that consumes a structured set of changelog rules and produces 1) a changelog fragment per rule and 2) a draft PR in the SDK monorepo with example code changes for each language.
3) Automated tests: snippet compilation/linting for each language and integration smoke tests against staging API.
4) UX review sign-off from Docs and DX teams and a security review if pipeline writes secrets (no secrets expected).
tasks:
- Design cookbook structure and recipe list (owner: Ayesha)
- Draft canonical examples in python, ts, go (owner: Liam)
- Implement transformation rules for common breaking patterns (owner: Priya Desai)
- Build changelog pipeline: rule parser -> snippet transformer -> PR generator (owner: Mateo Ruiz)
- Add CI jobs to validate generated snippets (owner: CI team)
- Docs deploy and QA (owner: Docs team)
- Post-launch monitoring: track migration PR adoption and snippet downloads (owner: Analytics)
design_notes_and_tradeoffs:
- We will prefer idiomatic examples per language rather than mechanical translation; that increases maintenance but reduces confusion for engineers migrating.
- For streaming ergonomics, Python will demonstrate both sync generator and async iterator patterns. TS will show AsyncIterable + Streams API. Go will show channel-based and streaming client examples.
- Retry semantics: adopt explicit idempotency token guidance as primary pattern; automatic retries will be shown but discouraged for non-idempotent operations. This avoids hidden duplicate side effects.
- Changelog pipeline: two modes — fast (text-only changelog fragments) and full (code snippet transformations + PR). Full mode is more complex but provides higher value; we'll ship fast mode first.
implementation_notes:
- Rules format: simple YAML with pattern matcher (regex) and per-language transform templates. Templates stored under /scripts/changelog-rules/*.yaml.
- PR generator uses GitHub API to open branch refs in sdk monorepo and commit snippets under docs/examples/migration/<lang>.
- Example generation will run in a restricted execution environment; snippets are not executed inside the rule engine to avoid injection. CI compiles/lints snippets post-PR.
- Use existing sdk-lint containers for Python/TS/Go to validate formatting and minimal import correctness.
- Keep transforms idempotent: running the pipeline multiple times should be a noop if the delta is already applied.

testing_plan:
- Unit tests for rule parser and template renderer.
- Snippet smoke tests: compile/format check for each language.
- End-to-end test in staging: run pipeline on a canned changelog diff and assert a PR appears with expected files.
- Load test: run PR generator at scale (200 rules) against a dry-run mode to check rate limits and concurrency.
- Manual QA: Docs reviewers will exercise each snippet in a short tutorial and sign off.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (fast): ship changelog fragment mode and python/ts examples to docs site behind feature flag.\nPhase 2 (full): enable PR generator for draft-only mode (no auto-merge) and invite internal SDK maintainers to review.\nPhase 3: GA with rate-limited automation and optional customer opt-in for example migration suggestions.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: Generated snippets contain incorrect imports or outdated API usage. Mitigation: strict CI lint/compile step blocking PR creation in full mode.\n- Risk: GitHub token misuse. Mitigation: bot token with narrow scope + rotation per security review.\n- Risk: Users rely on generated migrations for complex integrations. Mitigation: add prominent guidance: 'Run migration examples locally and run integration tests; generated snippets are suggestions.'
